note: Attacker-controlled TLS record bytes are written into the client's input BIO.
The client processes the crafted ServerHello and ServerKeyExchange handshake messages.
The DHE ServerKeyExchange message is dispatched to tls_process_ske_dhe.
The attacker-supplied DH prime, generator and public key are parsed from the packet.
Ownership of the DH object is transferred to peer_tmp; dh must no longer be freed directly.
The 64-bit DH prime yields 0 security bits (< 80), so the security check fails and control jumps to err.
The DH object is freed even though it is still owned by peer_tmp.
Freeing peer_tmp invokes evp_pkey_free_legacy -> DH_free on the already-freed DH object.
Second free of the same DH object: CRYPTO_DOWN_REF performs a WRITE 4 on freed memory, causing the heap-use-after-free.
